Concept illustration, not a live product capture. Local presentation draft.01 / 08

Every offer begins with the same question: what actually fits this home? Rhythm gives the planner a first draft they can inspect, change and explain. The goal is a better starting point for the next customer conversation.

RhythmThe problem

Missing inputs matter more
than another decimal.

A model can reproduce an installer’s patterns.
It cannot recover facts the customer has never supplied.

01

How much roof is usable?

Constrain the proposal instead of guessing the roof.

02

Is the annual consumption real?

Preserve the difference between entered and default.

03

Is an electric car planned?

Separate today’s household from tomorrow’s scenario.

Local evidence: docs/PITCH.md §3 and research/rhythm-findings.md. Missing-input questions are workflow proposals, not measured uplift.02 / 08

Our historical analysis found a missing-information problem: roof capacity is absent, consumption may be a default, and an EV flag does not capture every future charging need. Bigger models cannot resolve those omissions. We want to make the assumptions visible and help the planner ask the useful question.

Do not quote a causal accuracy improvement from asking these questions. The oracle experiment and Ask-next implementation are not verified complete.

Deterministic sizing and simulation. Language assistance is not the sizing engine.
Source inspection: TASK3-COMPATIBILITY-VERIFIED.md. Full joint optimization and complete BOM export are not claimed here.03 / 08

The expert target was reconstructed from line items, so units and parts interpretation matter before modelling. We learn installer-style choices, then add an hourly view of the energy economics. These are two different questions: what an expert offered, and what the simulation suggests. The planner should be able to see both.

The LLM never sizes the system. Do not claim completed manufacturer pairing checks or a fully implemented joint optimizer.

Pinned selection.test snapshot: 2026-11-07 18:59:49 UTC. M1, PV gate 0.6. Matching a recorded design is not proof of optimal sizing.04 / 08

Here is the result we can defend. The validation-selected model improves PV matching from 42.5 to 56.3 percent compared with the installer median: 13.8 percentage points on 325 later projects. It does not win every metric. Overall expert-match score and whole-design accuracy are lower than that median baseline.

We report the selected model, not the model with the most attractive test result. These numbers are a frozen existing evaluation artifact, not a fresh experiment. The appendix exposes all compared models. Do not claim statistical significance or a confidence interval without project-level paired analysis.

Switch to the actual application. Use a prepared synthetic case, explicitly labelled. Change annual demand from an illustrative 4,500 to 6,500 kWh, keeping other fields fixed. Show the real difference. If rehearsed, pin the battery and repeat an input change. Finally open the homeowner curve, using the share route only if it has passed rehearsal.

Only demonstrate the steps verified in rehearsal. Do not promise a wallbox, price delta or unchanged lock before observing the response. If the app is unavailable, stay on this slide and explain the sequence as planned behavior. A fallback recording has not been created by this deck.

The useful promise is not perfect certainty. It is being clear about what is known, estimated and still missing. Today the inspected engine can generate battery trade-off curves. The next step is ranking missing questions by design impact. That is a proposed experiment, not a completed feature or measured accuracy gain.

Explain the extra cost of the next battery size alongside its additional simulated benefit. Do not say a range is calibrated unless actual coverage evidence supports it.

RhythmA supporting engineering detail

a concrete rule.

The same battery family can need a different minimum stack.

BYD HVM · single tower

Permitted with PLENTICORE G3 under the cited matrix conditions.

≠
same rule
BYD HVM · single tower

4 modules · 11.04 kWh

Minimum in the listed Symo GEN24 Plus, ET 5–10 and STP Smart Energy pairings.

Research: documented pairings. Current engine: size snapping. Pair checks are not implemented.
BYD BCU2.0 V2.22, 2026-10-10. Exact models/firmware apply. Research is not installation approval. See TASK3-COMPATIBILITY-VERIFIED.md.07 / 08

One small example shows why compatibility needs more than a battery size dropdown. BYD’s current matrix permits a three-module HVM stack for PLENTICORE G3, while the other listed families start at four modules, under specified firmware conditions.

We have verified this as manufacturer research. The current engine snaps numerical sizes; it does not enforce that manufacturer matrix. Keep this point modest and honest.

Proposed pilot. Time savings, conversion and trust gains are not yet measured.

Rhythm · Home Energy Designer · thinc! München 202608 / 08

Our result is a useful first draft with a visible trade-off, rather than a claim that every historical decision is predictable. The next step is a pilot with a third installer on future projects. Measure what the planner changes, how long review takes, and whether the homeowner understands the offer. That is how we turn a promising demo into evidence of practical value.
